title: Priyanka Chopra Jonas Premieres 'The Cycle of Love' Documentary in New York
excerpt: The Oscar-winning documentary tells the true story of P.K. Mahanandia, a Dalit street artist from Delhi who cycled 6,000 miles to Sweden in the 1970s to reunite with the woman he loved.
body:
• The Cycle of Love, executive produced by Priyanka Chopra Jonas, premiered at the Directors Guild of America Theatre in Manhattan this week ahead of its August 28 theatrical release.
  • The documentary follows P.K. Mahanandia, a 23-year-old Dalit street artist who cycled roughly 6,000 miles from Delhi to Sweden in 1977 to reunite with Swedish student Lotta von Schedvin.
  • Directed by Academy Award winner Orlando von Einsiedel (The White Helmets, Virunga), the film blends real interviews with the couple and dramatic recreations filmed at original locations.
  • The film releases in U.S. theaters on August 28, with a UK release scheduled for September 18.

A Red-Carpet Premiere and a 50-Year Love Story

Priyanka Chopra Jonas walked the red carpet at the Directors Guild of America Theatre in Manhattan this week for the New York premiere of The Cycle of Love, a documentary she executive produced that tells one of the most remarkable real-life love stories to emerge from India in the 20th century.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=9W6JGhoTYjM

The film chronicles the journey of P.K. Mahanandia, a young Dalit street artist from Delhi who, in 1977, set off on a second-hand bicycle with nothing but a handful of paintbrushes, crossing nearly a dozen countries over roughly 6,000 miles to reach Sweden and reunite with Lotta von Schedvin — a 19-year-old Swedish traveller who had visited India and asked him to draw her portrait.

"I was just always fascinated with doing something this insane gesture of love that sounds almost unbelievable but isn't. And now, 50 years later, your kids are making a movie about your parents' love life, which is just so poignant and such a full journey."

— Priyanka Chopra Jonas, at the New York premiere

From Delhi Pavement to Oscar-Winning Director

Directed by Orlando von Einsiedel, whose credits include the Academy Award-winning short film The White Helmets and the Oscar-nominated feature Virunga, The Cycle of Love had its world premiere at the Telluride Film Festival, where it received standing ovations at every screening. Variety called it "one of the most romantic documentaries in years."

https://x.com/AP/status/2090886979407761474

The production team spent time on location, retracing the original route with Mahanandia himself joining for authenticity. Actor Chirag Benedict Lobo portrays the younger Mahanandia, while Norwegian actor Mina Dale plays the young von Schedvin. All scenes were improvised — there were no scripted lines.

"Everything was improvised. There were no lines at all. And we travelled and we were in the places where the actual events happened," Dale said of the production process.

A Story That Transcends Borders

Von Einsiedel chose to use Mahanandia's journey as a lens for broader themes of caste, culture, faith, and human connection rather than a straightforward biographical account. The route took the real Mahanandia through Afghanistan, Iran, Turkey, and across Europe — a journey shaped not just by love but by the barriers the world placed before him as a man from an "untouchable" family.

"Our film tells the extraordinary story of PK Mahanandia's journey in search of love despite the world being stacked against him," von Einsiedel said. "It's a thrilling and epic adventure about human connection and kindness, and a story that I believe transcends borders and nationalities."

The film was produced by the couple's children — Emelie Mahanandia von Schedvin and Karl Mahanandia von Schedvin — alongside Harri Grace and Chloe Leland. Sales rights were acquired by Dogwoof, the documentary distribution company, with BD4, Banijay America's premium production label, handling sales.

The Priyanka Connection

Chopra Jonas, who came on board through her production company Purple Pebble Pictures alongside producer Anne Carey, has spoken about her personal connection to the story. At the premiere, she drew a playful parallel to her own cross-cultural marriage to musician Nick Jonas.

"My husband got his bride from India, and he flew probably first class, so I don't know, it's very different. He had it way easier — I think PK had to really... it took him five months to get to his lady, right?" she joked.

Producer Emelie Mahanandia von Schedvin noted that Chopra Jonas connected personally with the story partly because "her husband is from another country as well and she's from India."

Where to Watch

The Cycle of Love opens in U.S. theaters on August 28 at the Angelika Film Center in New York City. A UK release follows on September 18, with additional international dates expected to be announced. For the Indian diaspora, the film offers a rare theatrical experience — a story born on a Delhi pavement, told by an Oscar-winning filmmaker, championed by one of India's biggest global stars, and rooted in the idea that determination and love know no boundaries.
image_caption: Priyanka Chopra Jonas at a recent public appearance promoting The Cycle of Love. The actress executive produced the documentary about an Indian street artist who cycled 6,000 miles to Sweden for love.
nri_angle: The film resonates deeply with the Indian diaspora experience — a cross-cultural love story spanning continents, produced by India's biggest global star, exploring themes of identity and belonging.
